chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa who said:

I made a copy of the letter in the possession of Ibn Rashid to the group of followers who reside in Baghdad, Madain, the Sawad, and surrounding areas: I praise Allah to you because of what I am in of good health granted by Him and His fair dealings with me. I invoke blessings upon His prophet and his family, the best of His blessings and most complete of His mercy and affection. I have appointed Aba Ali b. Rashid to take the place of Ali b. al-Husayn b. Abd Rabbi and whoever came before him from among my agents, and he has attained the same status the latter had with me. I give him authority over all that which the other agents had authority over among you so that he can collect my dues. I have chosen him for you and have given him precedence over others in this regard because he is the most suited and deserving of that. So fall in line – may Allah have mercy on you – in handing that over to him and to me, and do not give him any reason to fault you over, for it is incumbent upon you to avoid that, and to hasten to the obedience of Allah, and to legitimize your wealth and preserve your blood.
and assist each other in righteousness and piety, and fear Allah so that you may be mercied, and hold onto the rope of Allah all together, and do not die except as Muslims.

I have equated obedience to him with my obedience and embarking upon disobedience to him with embarking upon my disobedience. So stick steadfastly to the path and Allah will reward you and increase you from his own grace, for Allah is expansive and generous with what He has, bountiful to his servants, merciful. You and us are in the safe-guard of Allah and His protection. It is my own handwriting, and I praise Allah effusively.
ai.seo_question: Who was appointed as the Imam's agent in Baghdad and what is the significance of this appointment?
ai.summary: This letter from the Imam appoints Abu Ali ibn Rashid as his agent in Iraq, replacing previous agents. The Imam emphasizes that obedience to the new agent is equivalent to obedience to the Imam himself, and urges the followers to pay their dues promptly to legitimize their wealth and preserve their lives, citing Quranic verses on piety and unity.
